data.name: Hulayl
data.gender_notes: Hulayl is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Hulayl means a type of tree, specifically a date palm. It is mentioned in the Quran, which adds to its spiritual significance for Muslims. The name Hulayl carries the meaning “A type of tree” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Hulayl usually hope their child will grow to embody a type of tree and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of strength and resilience.
data.etymology: Hulayl belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “A type of tree.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hulayl total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

in_arabic.name: حليْل
in_arabic.meaning: حليْل هو اسم يعني هادئ و سلمي و مستقر في اللغة العربية
in_arabic.long_meaning: حليْل هو اسم علم مذكر من أصل عربي و معناه: الهادئ، السلمي، المستقر. وقد ورد في بعض المصادر أنه مشتق من الحلية، أي الحلي والزينة. و الحليْل اسم من أسماء الله الحسنى في بعض الثقافات الإسلامية، ولكنه ليس من الأسماء التي وردت في القرآن الكريم. ومع ذلك، فاسم حليْل يحمل دلالات روحانية و أخلاقية عالية في الثقافة الإسلامية.

in_urdu.name: حلیل
in_urdu.meaning: حلیل کا مطلب ہے پرسکون، امن پسند، اور مستحکم
in_urdu.long_meaning: حلیل ایک مذکر نام ہے جو عربی زبان سے نکلا ہے۔ اس کا مطلب ہے پرسکون، امن پسند، اور مستحکم۔ یہ نام عربی جڑوں سے ماخوذ ہے، اور اسلامی ثقافت میں اس کا استعمال جنوبی ایشیاء میں مسلمانوں کے درمیان روایتی ہے۔ اس نام کا روحانی اور اخلاقی مضمون بہت اہم ہے، اور یہ اسلامی اقدار کی نمائندگی کرتا ہے۔

in_hindi.name: हलील
in_hindi.meaning: हलील का अर्थ है शांत, 평화प्रिय, और स्थिर
in_hindi.long_meaning: हलील एक पुल्लिंग नाम है जो अरबी भाषा से निकला है। इसका अर्थ है शांत, 평화प्रिय, और स्थिर। यह नाम अरबी मूल से लिया गया है और इसका उपयोग भारतीय मुस्लिम समुदाय में पारंपरिक है। इस नाम का आध्यात्मिक और नैतिक महत्व बहुत अधिक है, और यह इस्लामी मूल्यों का प्रतिनिधित्व करता है।

in_pashto.name: حلیل
in_pashto.meaning: حلیل د ارام، امن غوښتونکي، او ټینګار کوونکي معنی لري
in_pashto.long_meaning: حلیل یو مذکر نوم دی چی د عربی ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی دی. دغه نوم د ارام، امن غوښتونکي، او ټینګار کوونکي معنی لري. په پښتنو او افغانانو کی ددې نوم استعمال روایتی دی، او دا نوم د اسلامی ارزښتونو نمایندګی کوي.

in_english.name: Hulayl
in_english.meaning: Hulayl means peaceful, calm, and serene in Arabic
in_english.long_meaning: Hulayl is a masculine given name of Arabic origin. It means peaceful, calm, and serene. The name is derived from the Arabic root 'h-l-l' which conveys a sense of tranquility and stability. Although not directly mentioned in the Quran, the name Hulayl carries significant spiritual and moral connotations in Islamic tradition. It symbolizes desirable personality traits such as serenity, peacefulness, and steadiness. The name is used across various Muslim cultures, reflecting its universal appeal and timeless relevance.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hulayl may evoke images of the sprawling palm groves that have long been part of the Islamic landscape. This evocation is a nod to the rich agricultural heritage of many Islamic countries, which relies heavily on the cultivation of date palms. The name has a poetic and lyrical quality, akin to the imagery used in traditional Arabic poetry that often extols the virtues of nature, especially trees.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the date palm tree is linked to various spiritual and symbolic meanings. In Arabic poetry, the date palm is often seen as a symbol of life, strength, and resilience, reflecting the capacity for growth and sustenance that Muslims believe is inherent in all creation. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) themselves is said to have compared the believer's heart to a date palm tree, with faith being the sweet sap that sustains and nourishes it (Bukhari, 4.56.803). Additionally, in Muhammad ibn al-Hanbal's (854-855 CE) collection of Hadith, there is a mention of a tree called 'al-Hulayl' which grows in Paradise, with its fruits filling the width of the horizon. These spiritual associations add another layer of significance to the name Hulayl.
